Theme

recycle verb

also recycling, recycling bin, recyclable, recycled

our formation

Verg. A. 7.636: recoquunt patriōs fornācibus ēnsēs (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 16.23

recoquō, recoquere, recoxī, recoctum

verb, third conjugation

cook again, melt down again: recycle

Our use: Morgan–Owens has a heading recycle with no Latin, and no other reference work has a word. Classically recoquere is to boil again, or to melt down and forge again (Lewis & Short), which is what is done with glass, metal and paper. The recycling bin: excipulum recoquendōrum.

Other words

  • regignō, regignere — beget again

    verb, third conjugation · also used · modern · Andresian pp. 2, 11: excipulum regignendōrum

    Andresian’s word for the recycling bin. Classically it occurs once, in Lucretius (5.244, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Lagoenam nē abjēcerīs; recoquētur.

    Don’t throw the bottle away; it’ll be recycled.composed

See also rubbish bin, bin bag, rubbish.

SourcesLewis & Short: recoquo · Lewis & Short: regigno

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. recycle, recycling (no Latin given).

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 2.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
